about: Round 1022. The two fact tables in src/lib/soccerCareerEngine.ts that a Soccer Career player sees as real: INT_SCORING_RECORDS (each nation's men's all time international scoring record, which decides the All Time Top Scorer award and its line) and the league label on every one of the 190 HAND_CLUBS rows (188 verified for the current season and 2 with no current table online yet; Round 1037 released the 7 once pinned to their old label, because every season before 2026-27 is now answered from the league ledgers). Every value here was read on the date beside it from two independent sources that agree, none of them Wikipedia. Where two sources disagreed a third settled it, and where nothing settled it the value is left out (intRecordsHeld): a nation with no verified row gets no award at all, there is no default. scripts/simCareerFacts.mjs holds the engine to this file and fails if either side moves. Records held by active players move with every international window, so each row carries asOf, the last date both sources were read; refresh them together, never one side.

Egypt.note: Mohamed Salah is on 68 and still active (last cap 2026-09-25, no goal; he missed the next two matches). A second counting line exists: Ahram Online, africasoccer.com and Al Shorouk (all before 2026-09-25) give Hassan 68 and Salah 67, a dispute over Hassan's own career count (rsssf: 69 in 177, excluding ten non-A matches). The gap is one goal on both lines. 69 is kept because it is the higher count: a career has to pass it to win the award, and a total above 69 is above Hassan on either line, so the line the game prints is true whichever count a reader trusts.

leagueWorld.about: Round 1100. One row a league label the career club pool is generated from (scripts/lib/careerClubPool.mjs POOL_LEAGUE_ROWS), for the season the label describes: 2026-27, or the calendar year 2026 for the Brasileirao and MLS. members is the league's clubs in the career's own spelling, compared name by name with Club Manager's lineup. membership: the two (or more) pages the lineup and the size were read from, on different hosts, none a wiki. format: the pages the shape and the number of games were read from; a league gets a size, a format and a cadence row, or an odd format row, only with two of them on different hosts. ESPN's feeds and BBC Sport's tables were read raw by script and compared by name; the prose pages are quoted. evidence names the leagueEvidence group Round 1022 read for the hand clubs of the same league, when there is one. unnamed: clubs of the league Club Manager does not carry, counted in the size and never named.

the club, on its 2021-22 home jersey: "honouring the colours synonymous with the region, the classic black and white"

clubSince.about: Round 1100. Since when the game offers each generated pool club. Every generated club has exactly one decision here. shipped: one of the 51 rows Round 1013 shipped; it stays in every era exactly as main had it (their first seasons were never two sourced: an open item, see scripts/simCareerClubPool.mjs). held: a club Round 1100 brought in. The game knows it as a 2026-27 club and nothing earlier, so it is not offered, drawn or met in any season before heldBefore until its first season as a professional club under this name is read from two sources that are not wikis; then it moves to since with that year (a year of 1990 or earlier means every era). Nothing here is a founding date and none is claimed. One place a held club is named earlier: a past league table. Where the Round 1036 league ledgers (scripts/data/leagueSeasons) hold the club in that league that season from two sources, that season's table and fixtures print its name; it is still not offered in the market, drawn in a continental tie or played as a derby before heldBefore.

clubCountries.about: Round 1100. Pool clubs whose country is not their league's (scripts/lib/careerClubPool.mjs CLUB_COUNTRY, beside the rows Club Manager's own clubCountry holds). Each one Round 1100 adds is read from two hosts; the three Welsh clubs shipped with Round 1013, read then from goal.com and footballgroundguide.com (2026-10-05, the generator's own comment).
